//: Why this file exists, and why four.
Every test class in this project that needs a database creates one and runs the
real migrator against it. That is deliberate -- a test that built its own tables
could pass while the shipped migration was broken -- and it means a whole-solution
run starts fourteen of these migrations at once in this assembly alone, beside
sixteen more in Gateway.Tests.
xUnit's default is one thread per core, which on the machine this was measured on
is twenty. The server answers that with 'failed to launch job ... out of background
workers' -- 24578 times in one log -- because max_worker_processes is 39 and every
parallel query and maintenance worker competes for those slots. What a test sees is
not that warning but its own client deadline: NpgsqlException: The operation has
timed out, inside ConnectAsync, in whichever test happened to be unlucky. It was
seen in MigrationLockTests, in EmbeddedScriptsTests, in DataProtectionKeysTests and
in a configuration-publishing test, which is the signature of a shared ceiling
rather than of any one test being wrong.
Four rather than a number chosen for how it feels: enough to keep the suite quick,
few enough that the migrations are not all at once. It is capped per assembly, so
the seven assemblies together still use the machine -- what is removed is the
thirty-at-once spike, not the parallelism.
This is not a fix for a product defect. The product has no such ceiling: it runs one
migrator (ADR-0014) and one Gateway. What this fixes is a test harness whose
parallelism outgrew the database it shares.
